copy.blurb:
A +7.7pp gap on the New Zealand side. New Zealand v Belgium in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has New Zealand stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Elo numbers going in: New Zealand 1550, Belgium 1860. That's a 310-point lead for Belgium — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: New Zealand to win at 13%, the draw at 11%, and Belgium to win at 76%. The home side reads 13% on this distribution — the model's central case for New Zealand.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: New Zealand to win at 5%, the draw at 12%, and Belgium to win at 82%. On the New Zealand side specifically the market reads 5%, which prices out at American odds of +1900. Compared against the model's 13%, that's the +7.7pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On New Zealand the lower bound is 9%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +4.5pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 35 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Pre-match Elo gives New Zealand a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +7.7pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the New Zealand side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On New Zealand, the model is +7.7pp out from Polymarket. Our number reads 13%; the market reads 5%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: New Zealand v Belgium · the model leans New Zealand
